chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he supplicates to his Lord while he is in prostration.
So, what do you say when you prostrate? I said, 'Teach me, may I be sacrificed for you!' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Say:'

'O Lord of the lords, and O King of the kings, and O Master of the masters, and O Compeller of the compellers, and O God of the gods! Send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and do such and such with me.'
Then say, 'I am Your servant, my forelock being in Your grip.'
Then supplicate with whatever you wish and ask Him, for He is Generous, and nothing is too great for Him.

key_terms.جَبَّارَ الْجَبَابِرَةِ: Compeller of the compellers, a divine attribute
key_terms.رَبَّ الْأَرْبَابِ: Lord of the lords, a title of majesty
key_terms.سَجْدٌ: Prostration, a position of worship in prayer
key_terms.نَاصِيَتِي: My forelock, symbolizing control or grip

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication formula to recite during prostration (sajdah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual proximity achieved during prostration, offering a structured supplication that begins with divine majesty (rububiyyah) and transitions to personal petition, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt. The instruction to follow the formula with 'ask for what you will' underscores God's boundless generosity (jawd), encouraging believers to view their needs as manageable for the Creator. This practice aligns with the theological concept that the physical act of sajda facilitates a direct, intimate connection with the Divine, free from worldly distractions.
